summary: SRI's Artificial Intelligence group reports plans to join the ARPANET after switching their PDP-10 to TENEX. The connection would go through the existing IMP at SRI and a PDP-15 controller, using TENEX network software where possible. A response to RFC 116.

plainLanguage.summary: SRI's Artificial Intelligence Group describes how it plans to join the ARPANET after changing its computer system. It expects to share research programs and use the network to contact other researchers.

sections.title: Preparing the SRI Connection
sections.content:
SRI's Artificial Intelligence Group expects to join the ARPANET as a research center after converting its PDP-10 to TENEX. It plans to connect through SRI's existing IMP, which already serves the Network Information Center, and use a PDP-15 to control peripherals.

The hardware interface was still being bid on. The group intended to reuse as much TENEX network software as possible and expected that changes might be limited to the hardware-oriented part of the Network Control Program.
sections.plainLanguage: SRI is changing its computer system before joining the network. It plans to reuse existing network software and connect through equipment already at SRI.

sections.title: Expected Services and Participation
sections.content:
The group's most optimistic estimate for functional network connection was mid-July 1971. It expected to support several outside users at once, with the system normally available during business hours and often at other times. Maintenance and hardware failures could interrupt service.

SRI expected to make research software available, including QA3.6, STRIPS and possibly QA4. The group also hoped to try artificial-intelligence programs from other sites and use the network for occasional contact with network participants.
sections.plainLanguage: SRI expected to share several research programs and support a few outside users at once. It also hoped to try programs from other sites and contact network participants.

sections.title: Current Work
sections.content: At the time of the report, system support staff were focused on hardware and design changes. The group's contact with the Network Working Group had therefore been limited. The authors thought participation might grow after the system became operational.
sections.plainLanguage: The team was busy preparing the hardware and had little time for network group work. It expected to take a larger part after the connection was working.
